records.title: BDR Enablement Lead
records.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
records.text: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We're looking for a BDR Enablement Lead to own the curriculum and craft development of Anthropic's business development organization. Our BDRs are the front door to the pipeline and, for many of them, this is the first serious sales role of their career. What they learn here shapes how they sell for the next decade. This role owns that formation: the onboarding curriculum, sales foundations, the ongoing skill development, and the pipeline generation playbooks that turn effort into meetings. It is also a role with an unusual opportunity. Anthropic's BDRs should be the most AI-native prospecting team in the industry. You will build the workflows that make that true — using plugins, account research skills, and agentic tooling to change what a BDR can accomplish in a day. Doing this well requires someone who is genuinely excited about the craft of prospecting and about rebuilding it around what AI now makes possible. Key responsibilities Own the BDR onboarding curriculum, taking new hires from day one to first meeting booked as quickly as we responsibly can Enable BDRs on AI-native prospecting workflows, including plugins, account research skills, and agentic tooling that meaningfully change BDR productivity Develop and maintain pipeline generation playbooks across segments, personas, and motions Run ongoing skill development on sales fundamentals: cold calling, written outreach, objection handling, discovery, and qualification Certify BDRs on our products, our qualification criteria, and our messaging Partner with BDR leadership to identify where skill gaps are constraining pipeline, and build focused interventions Build the coaching and call-review infrastructure that gives BDRs specific, frequent feedback Measure enablement impact on ramp time, activity quality, meeting conversion, and pipeline contribution Create a clear development path from BDR into the next role, in partnership with sales leadership Minimum qualifications Experience in Enablement, including time as a high-performing BDR or BDR manager Have excelled in the role you are now enabling, and are passionate about mentorship and early-career development Are excited about rebuilding the prospecting motion around AI rather than bolting AI onto the old one Are hands-on with prospecting tooling and willing to build workflows yourself rather than specifying them for someone else Can teach the unglamorous fundamentals with energy, and can model them on a live call Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and enjoy building from 0 to 1 Care about the person as much as the number, and can hold both Are technically curious about AI and credible talking about our products with a technical audience Preferred qualifications Have 8+ years of experience in Enablement, including time as a high-performing BDR or BDR manager Hand-on experience with Claude Cowork, Claude Code, and other Claude surfaces Experience collaborating across global and cross-functional teams Experience building 0-1 onboarding programs and discovery frameworks Experience designing or operating a BDR-to-AE promotion path Hands-on experience building prospecting automations, agents, or internal tooling Experience enabling BDRs across multiple segments or regions A track record connecting BDR enablement to measurable pipeline outcomes The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $190,000 — $270,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. records.title: Cloud Partner Enablement Lead
records.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
records.text: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role Anthropic is looking for a Partner Enablement leader to own how we enable our cloud partner ecosystem. Claude reaches a significant share of enterprise customers through AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, and the sellers, solution architects, and delivery teams inside those organizations are often the first people a customer talks to about deploying frontier AI. This role makes sure they are ready. You will translate Anthropic's product and go-to-market strategy into repeatable programs that help cloud partner field teams find, qualify, and win Claude opportunities, and then deliver them well. That means building the enablement infrastructure end to end: onboarding, launch readiness, sales and technical training, certification pathways, co-sell playbooks, and the metrics that tell us whether any of it is working. The job runs in both directions, and internal enablement is a sizable portion of it. Just as important as readying partner field teams is making sure Anthropic's own GTM organization knows how to work with the hyperscalers: which partnerships we have and what each one actually covers, how co-sell and marketplace mechanics differ across the three providers, when to pull a partner into a deal, and the offering nuances that determine what we can and cannot do through each channel. This is a build role as much as a run role. Cloud partner enablement at Anthropic is early, so you will be designing the operating model at the same time as you are shipping against a fast launch cadence. You will work closely with Partnerships, Applied AI, Product Marketing, Sales, and each hyperscaler's own partner and enablement organizations. Responsibilities You will own the cloud partner enablement strategy across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, defining what "ready" means for each partner motion and building the programs that get partner field teams there. That starts with the co-sell motion: you will build the playbooks that let partner sellers carry Claude into enterprise deals alongside our own team, and you will make sure those assets map to how each hyperscaler's marketplace and co-sell mechanics actually work. You will design and run scalable enablement programs rather than one-off training. That includes onboarding paths for new cloud partner teams, role-based learning journeys for sellers and a repeatable launch readiness motion so partner teams are current on every new model and capability we ship. This work runs in both directions. You will also enable Anthropic's own GTM team, making sure sellers and partner-facing staff know which cloud partnerships we have and what each one covers, how co-sell and marketplace mechanics differ across the three providers, when to bring a partner into a deal, and the offering nuances that shape what we can do through each channel. Keeping the field current as those agreements and offerings change is a standing part of the job. You will build the content and the systems behind it, curating what lives in our partner portal and learning platforms, establishing review and refresh governance so nothing goes stale, and creating enablement assets that hold up in front of technical and commercial audiences alike. You will also partner directly with the enablement and partner development teams inside each cloud provider to land Anthropic content inside their channels, which is how this work reaches scale. Finally, you will instrument the program. You will define the metrics that connect enablement activity to partner-sourced pipeline, certification attainment, and deal velocity. records.text: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Beneficial Deployments team accelerates the work of organizations doing some of the world's most important under-resourced work: nonprofits, education institutions, scientific researchers, and organizations advancing economic mobility. Education institutions sit at the center of that mission. They train the next generation, they produce the science the rest of the world builds on, and they are structurally short on time, budget, and technical capacity to figure out new technology on their own. You will lead our targeted approach to higher education, with a specific focus on research institutes, research intensive universities, and schools focused on access like community colleges and MSIs. You will also support K12 staff and educators across the globe, in particular in low and middle income countries, where teachers and school staff are the users and the district is often the buyer. Where our scaled motion reaches thousands of organizations one to many, this role is the opposite end of the same ecosystem: a deliberately short list of institutions where depth matters, where a lab, a department, or a whole campus adopting Claude changes what science gets done, and where the buying process runs through provosts, research offices, district superintendents, procurement, grant budgets, and security review. Reach comes first, and commercial results follow from it. That ordering is deliberate and it is shared across every leader on this team: a research institute that adopts Claude to move its science faster is a win on its own terms, and you will be measured on creating that value with the institutions that matter most, not only on pipeline. You are the single accountable owner for the research and education Enterprise book globally: its target list, its AEs, its numbers, and its field voice inside Anthropic. You are half seller, half domain translator. You will personally run the most complex institutional deals, and you will be credible in a room of scientists and educators. You know how research is funded, how a university decides, and what it takes for an education sales motion to land in a software company. You will bring that knowledge to the product, applied AI, and marketing teams who build for this audience. This is a player coach seat. You will be directly involved in deals and directing the account executives who cover education today, and the role is expected to grow thoughtfully with more AEs in key regions globally. Key responsibilities scientific discovery and economic access, support for K12 staff and educators Serve as the lead on our most complex institutional deals — setting the pursuit strategy, opening doors with lab and research-office leadership, university provosts, and personally resolving the toughest hurdles: procurement, security review, and grant-funded budgets. Direct and coach the account executives working education accounts today: joint account plans, deal reviews, and a repeatable motion for landing a university and expanding within it. Build the institutional playbook: how an institute goes from a pilot to a working deployment across a department, what good adoption looks like, and when to bring in applied AI, customer success, or partners. Own the book's numbers, institutions reached, activated, and expanded against goals, and use them to decide where the effort goes next. Work in lockstep with our PLG 1:many motion, so that an institution moves cleanly between scaled programs and direct coverage in both directions. Minimum qualifications Education or research sales. You have sold software as a service into universities, research institutes, or academic medical centers, and you have personally closed complex institutional agreements involving procurement, security review, and multiple decision makers. Science or education background. You have trained or worked in a scientific field, or spent a meaningful part of your career selling to or building for scientists or educators, and you can hold a credible conversation with these audiences. Sales leadership. You have led a sales business end to end and been the accountable owner for its results, whether as a team lead, a player coach, or the sole owner of a strategic book. Preferred qualifications Global education landscape: experience selling to universities, research institutes, or school systems in more than one region, an understanding of how funding and procurement differ from country to country, and comfort working across time zones with regional teams. Experience with research funding: grants, indirect costs, and how a fixed annual budget shapes what an institution can buy. Track record landing an institution wide agreement at a research intensive university, and expanding from a single department to a campus or system. Familiarity with how AI is already used in research settings and K12 classrooms, and a point of view on where it should go next. Experience working with academic consortia, national labs, or research networks. An impact, education, research, or mission driven go to market background, and genuine interest in these institutions' constraints. A daily working habit with Claude, and agentic workflows you have built for yourself. You might thrive here if You want your work measured in impact that moves faster and students who get more from their education, not only in pipeline. You have sat in a faculty meeting or a research office and know why the obvious commercial playbook does not work there. You are comfortable being the only person accountable for a book while depending on teams you do not manage. You would rather close the first three institutional deals yourself and write the playbook from what you learned than write the strategy deck first. You find the constraint interesting rather than frustrating: long procurement cycles, grant timelines, and security reviews are the job, not an obstacle to it. This is a highly cross-functional role. You'll partner with GTM leadership, hiring managers, Revenue Operations, Marketing, and product teams to keep the program current as our products and sales motions evolve. records.text: Role Summary HubSpot Academy is on a mission to be the place people go to learn how to start and grow a business. We offer a variety of educational and inspirational content — from lessons and full certification courses to live, hands-on workshops — that provides valuable business training to people all over the world. This educational content generates new customers for the business and delights our existing ones in service of achieving their business and career goals. We're looking for a Professional HubSpot Academy Professor - Coach who is passionate about helping customers confidently use HubSpot tools through live, hands-on small group coaching sessions. This role is ideal for someone who shows growing independence and proficiency in live facilitation and content creation, effectively applying skills to enhance customer outcomes while contributing to HubSpot's educational mission at scale. As a Professional HubSpot Academy Professor - Coach at HubSpot Academy, you'll be responsible for developing and delivering live, small group coaching sessions focused on specific HubSpot tools and use cases, as well as creating supporting on-demand educational content. You'll design engaging workshop experiences and practical learning resources that solve real customer problems, drive product adoption, and support long-term usage of HubSpot products. The role requires good understanding of adult learning principles, live facilitation skills, content creation abilities, and comprehensive knowledge of HubSpot's product offerings, as well as a passion for crafting hands-on learning experiences that deliver measurable impact at scale. This role sits on the HubSpot Academy team and reports to the Manager of HubSpot Academy Education. You'll work alongside other Academy Professors and Customer Evangelists to develop comprehensive educational strategies that align with HubSpot's business objectives and support customers at scale. What you'll do: Facilitate High-Impact Small Group Coaching Sessions: Lead multiple live, interactive coaching sessions each week for groups of customers focused on specific HubSpot tools, features, or use cases (e.g., Advanced CRM, Marketing Automation, Customer Agent, Loop Marketing plays) Run sessions in alignment with standardized agendas and learning objectives while adapting to the needs and questions of each cohort in real-time Demonstrate growing expertise in facilitating workshops where customers work on their real HubSpot challenges and leave having configured something concrete in their portal Create supportive learning environments where customers feel comfortable asking questions, sharing use cases, and learning from peers Create Supporting On-Demand Content: Develop short educational videos, workbooks, and guides that complement small group coaching topics and enable customers to review key concepts Create practical resources that customers can reference when implementing what they learned during coaching sessions Design follow-up materials that reinforce session learning and support continued product adoption Collaborate with Instructional Designers and content creators to ensure cohesive learning experiences across live and on-demand formats Drive Product Adoption and Usage Uplift: Design sessions and supporting content so customers leave with actionable next steps and concrete configurations in their HubSpot portals Partner cross-functionality to understand which specific actions and sessions drive the largest usage movement Refine content and facilitation approaches based on data showing what drives measurable customer outcomes Track how coaching sessions contribute to customer activation, feature adoption, and ongoing product usage Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Work closely with Academy, Product, Creative, and Marketing teams to align session topics with product launches, spotlight moments, and strategic initiatives (e.g., AI adoption, Loop Marketing, Customer Agent) Provide structured feedback to Product and leadership on what customers are saying and where they're getting stuck Ensure coaching insights inform product roadmap and enablement priorities Participate in cross-functional projects to develop educational strategies aligned with business goals Maintain Operational Excellence: Ensure accurate logging of sessions and attendance via Bevy and HubSpot systems, partnering with operations teams to resolve data integrity issues Follow established workflows for customer inquiries about registration, scheduling, or follow-up questions Use tools like Asana, AirTable, and Google Suite to coordinate session planning, content development, and track key metrics Monitor registration and attendance patterns to optimize session timing, topics, and promotional approaches Continuously Improve Content and Experience: Iterate on session content, flow, and activities based on NPS, CSAT, qualitative feedback, and performance metrics (attendance, usage impact, repeat attendance) Collect session feedback to continuously improve both live facilitation and supporting on-demand content Experiment with new formats (e.g., "Build With" sessions, customer guest speakers, region-specific variants) Share insights with the broader team to enhance the small group coaching program and on-demand content library What you'll bring: Required Qualifications Fluency in French and Portuguese You have demonstrated experience leading live trainings, workshops, or group sessions (virtual or in-person) where you taught, demoed, and troubleshooted on the fly. You possess exceptional facilitation and communication skills—you can read a room, simplify complex topics, and keep diverse audiences engaged and on track. You have strong product aptitude and quickly learn new features, connecting them to real-world customer use cases across Marketing, Sales, and Service workflows. You effectively communicate and collaborate with customers and cross-functional teams to align on coaching objectives and customer needs. You're energized by scale—reaching hundreds or thousands of customers through repeatable experiences—and see group coaching as core to the future of customer education. You're customer-obsessed and empathetic, able to meet customers where they are in their journey, even when they're just beginning with advanced features. You comfortably adjust to changing priorities in a fast-evolving environment where programs, tools, and processes are being optimized, and you actively contribute to improvements. You can craft well-structured written content for workbooks, guides, and supporting materials that enhance learning experiences. You independently explore and suggest innovative approaches to coaching and content creation, experimenting with new facilitation techniques and formats. Nice to Have: Experience working directly with HubSpot (as a user, partner, or prior HubSpotter), especially across multiple Hubs Experience facilitating global customer audiences across time zones Familiarity with event platforms, and/or prior experience in scaled programs or live onboarding Experience creating short-form video content or educational materials Pay & Benefits The cash compensation below includes base salary, on-target commission for employees in eligible roles, and annual bonus targets under HubSpot’s bonus plan for eligible roles. records.text: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies — from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups — use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Stripe's Financial Crimes, Compliance and Risk Oversight (FinCRO) organisation serves as Stripe's second line of defense, ensuring we operate as a responsible steward of the global financial ecosystem. You will join the Product and User Enablement (ProUse) team within FinCRO, acting as a trusted compliance advisor to our first line business teams (e.g., GTM, Risk, Ops) to help scale business and grow our user base globally. What you’ll do We are looking for an experienced compliance advisor who is fluent in both compliance regulations and commercial reality. You will not just be a specialized advisor, but a strategic partner responsible for scaling our business by embedding compliance intelligence directly into our technical infrastructure to support our users. You will be the bridge between Stripe’s compliance obligations and our users' ambitious goals, moving away from manual, person-dependent models toward a dynamic, agentic structure. You will provide expert guidance for our complex user challenges to actively shape them. You will partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders to design user solutions that both support users' growing journey with Stripe and satisfy compliance rigor. Stripe is both a technology company and a financial services company. You will need to be comfortable straddling those worlds every day, moving quickly in the face of ambiguity to help scale our business globally. Responsibilities: You will be a critical team member responsible for: Partner deeply with GTM and business teams for complex user deals to identify compliance roadblocks early and design the "path to yes" that aligns with our risk appetite. Lead compliance reviews and risk assessments for material user matters, providing clear, risk-based recommendations. Influence business roadmaps and design decisions, translating compliance requirements into clear, actionable product, control, and reporting expectations. Lead with a first-principles approach, bringing sound judgment to novel user-related questions and helping teams identify practical, sustainable paths forward. Deploy strategically as a subject matter expert to explain intricate compliance requirements to users and first line teams with authority, clarity, and empathy. Work with users and internal teams to architect solutions and flows that meet compliance obligations while minimizing friction. Work closely with Regional Compliance Officers, Money Laundering Reporting Officers, Legal, and other SMEs to support execution across complex, cross-functional user supportability designs. Help business teams build durable compliance capabilities by making established requirements, precedents, and standards easy to understand and apply independently, driving a “compliant by design” approach. Leverage AI and agentic tools to scale user enablement - including accelerating risk assessments, regulatory research, and requirements documentation - while applying rigorous judgment to novel, complex, or precedent-setting decisions and validating AI-generated outputs. Who you are Minimum Requirements 9+ years of experience building and managing compliance programs in regulated financial services, preferably in fintech, payments, or banking. Strong knowledge of regulatory compliance and financial crimes/AML practices, with an understanding of the risk landscape applicable to a company like Stripe. Proven ability to independently lead multiple complex projects and programs, from ambiguous early questions through implementation. Ability to interpret regulations and regulatory guidance, identify the underlying risks they are intended to address, and translate those requirements into comprehensive, proportionate compliance programs. Experience evaluating complex user requests for compliance risk and working with business stakeholders to implement creative solutions to enable users while meeting compliance requirements Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex compliance concepts into clear, commercial language for different stakeholders across the business, as well as with users directly Excellent cross-functional collaboration skills, including navigating leadership and interpersonal working relationships Intellectual curiosity and comfort operating at the frontier, including exploring unfamiliar markets, product types, and regulatory frameworks. Sound, independent judgment in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment. Genuine interest in financial product innovation and an eagerness to drive the industry forward by building and scaling products responsibly. Lead compliance reviews and product risk assessments for material new launches and feature expansions, providing clear, risk-based recommendations. Support product governance efforts and Board engagement, including documenting and presenting product requirements and tracking implementation. Lead with a first-principles approach, bringing sound judgment to novel product questions and helping teams identify practical, sustainable paths forward. Work closely with Regional Compliance Officers, Money Laundering Reporting Officers, Legal, and other SMEs to support execution across complex, cross-functional product designs. records.title: Program Manager, Risk Operations GTM Enablement
records.text: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team The Risk PMO team protects Stripe’s revenue and drives cross-functional strategy for company-level and org-level priorities. As Stripe operates across an increasingly complex and fast-moving global regulatory environment, one of our most important functions is ensuring that our largest, most strategic users can grow with us—compliantly, confidently, and at speed. We sit at the intersection of Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Product, Data Science, and GTM—serving as the bridge between teams coordinating massive programs with global, wide-reaching impact. We build durable systems that enable strong collaboration across functions and seamless experiences for our users. If you're energized by high-stakes, ambiguous problems and thrive on building programs from scratch in environments where the rules are still being written—we want to hear from you. What you’ll do You will define, own, and execute program strategies for large-scale regulatory initiatives, operating with significant autonomy across a portfolio of global projects. This is a highly visible, senior individual contributor (IC) role. While you will influence senior leadership and set strategic direction, you are also the primary driver of execution. You will need to zoom out to design the long-term vision, and zoom in to manage the details—building templates, tracking deliverables, writing documentation, and directly unblocking cross-functional teams. Responsibilities Own and execute high-stakes global programs end-to-end, from initial strategy and scoping to project planning, day-to-day tracking, and change management Drive step-change improvements in our operational processes, rolling up your sleeves to build systems and workflows that directly improve business outcomes and top-line metrics Bridge compliance and commercial strategy by partnering with GTM and account leadership to turn complex regulatory requirements into a competitive advantage that builds deep user trust Build and run operating models across diverse cross-functional teams (including Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, and Compliance), keeping highly distributed workstreams aligned and accountable Serve as a trusted advisor by preparing strategic reviews for senior stakeholders and managing critical escalations Translate user friction into program evolution by establishing structured, data-driven approaches to gather user feedback and turning those insights into actionable product and operational improvements Diagnose and resolve systemic operational gaps before they impact our users, building self-healing processes and scalable internal infrastructure Champion Stripe’s Operating Principles by fostering a high-performance culture that values rigorous thinking, rapid execution, and putting users first Who you are You are a highly strategic operator, a masterful communicator, and a systems thinker with operational grit. You thrive in the gray area, possessing the ability to translate ambiguous global challenges into elegant, structured, and highly actionable operational frameworks. You are a natural leader who leads by influence and by example. You have a deep empathy for the user, an unyielding bias toward action, and you take pride in the craft of execution. No problem is too complex for you to deconstruct, and no detail is too small if it impacts the user experience. Minimum requirements 6+ years of experience in Program Management, Strategy & Operations, Management Consulting, or Go-to-Market (GTM) Strategy in a fast-paced, high-growth environment Hands-on execution track record: Proven ability to work independently as an individual contributor, managing complex, multi-stakeholder project plans and deliverables from inception to completion Exceptional communication & storytelling: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; a proven ability to distill highly complex, technical, or regulatory topics into clear, succinct, and persuasive narratives to external and senior audiences Systems and infrastructure builder: Deep experience designing, launching, and scaling complex cross-functional operating models, feedback loops, and PMO frameworks Growth mindset: A high willingness to learn, adapt quickly to changing environments, and actively seek and act on feedback to continuously improve Preferred qualifications 3+ years of experience in high-growth technology or fintech environments Deep cross-functional partnership: Prior experience working alongside Engineering, Product, Legal, Compliance, and GTM/Sales Data fluency: Experience leveraging data visualization tools and analytical frameworks to back up strategic decisions and measure program success

records.text: About the Team The Scaling team is responsible for the architectural and engineering backbone of OpenAI’s infrastructure. We design and deliver advanced systems that support the deployment and operation of cutting-edge AI models. Our work spans system software, networking, platform architecture, fleet-level monitoring, and performance optimization. About the Role We’re hiring an SW Engineer to enable production workloads and end-to-end testing on new platforms. This role will include creating new test harnesses and platform stress benchmarks, porting existing inference and training workloads to new, sometimes early-access, systems/hardware, analyzing performance and bottlenecks, and characterizing the end-to-end behavior of new systems (compute, comms, storage, control plane, and failure modes). Key Responsibilities Port and validate key inference and training workloads on new platforms/SKUs as they arrive; drive correctness, performance, and stability to an internal readiness bar. Build a suite of benchmarks and stress tests that capture real E2E behavior of our workloads by exercising all aspects of a system, including CPU, GPU, memory subsystem, frontend, scale-up, and scale-out networking (including WAN traffic, NVlink and RDMA collectives), storage, thermals, and any other relevant parts. Deep-dive performance on distributed training/inference: Collective performance and tuning (across NCCL/RCCL and internal libraries) Overlap of compute/communication, kernel-level bottlenecks, memory bandwidth and scheduling effects Create repeatable test harnesses that run in CI / lab environments and produce actionable outputs (pass/fail, performance score, regression detection). Partner with systems + fleet bring-up engineers to ensure the platform is not only stable and performant, but also operationally usable and scalable (containerization, K8s integration, telemetry hooks, failure triage loops). Work cross-functionally with vendors and internal stakeholders by producing clear bug reports, minimal repros, and prioritized issue lists. Qualifications BS in CS/EE (or equivalent practical experience). 5+ years in one or more of: ML systems, performance engineering, distributed systems, or HPC. Strong profiling/debugging skills (e.g., Nsight, rocprof, perf, flamegraphs; ability to reason from traces/counters). records.text: About the team The Agent Enablement Applied AI Engineering team works across engineering, product, design, partnerships, and strategic customers to grow an open ecosystem of agent-enabled sites and services. We help partners adopt the OpenAI tech stack related to identity, permissioning, agent-auth primitives so users can safely connect ChatGPT and Codex to the tools, services, and workflows they already use. This is a hands-on, partner-facing product engineering role for someone who can contribute to the platform itself, lead sophisticated technical engagements, and turn ambiguous identity and agent-workflow requirements into secure, production-ready integrations. You will work across partner product and engineering teams and OpenAI’s product, engineering, design, partnerships, legal, policy, security, support, and go-to-market teams. You will identify high-value user journeys, choose the right integration path, prototype and review architectures, write code, run evaluations and dogfood, trace failures end to end, guide launch and rollout, and support post-launch iteration. The best person for this role moves fluidly between full-stack code, OAuth/OIDC and identity systems, product judgment, project leadership, and clear communication with engineers and executives. This role is a fit for a product-minded engineer who wants to stay close to users and partners while going deep on authentication, permissions, reliability, safety, and developer experience. The principle objective is to help partners ship low-friction, trustworthy agent experiences that work across real-world account states, enterprise constraints, and user expectations. This role is based in our San Francisco office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Help partners choose and implement the right integration path across browser sign-in, connector-initiated OAuth, and agentic account linking or provisioning, with clear user journeys and safe fallback behavior. Write production and sample code, build reference implementations and test harnesses, and create the technical guidance, integration checklists, evaluations, and debugging tools that move partners from concept to production. Contribute targeted improvements to ChatGPT, Codex, and the Agent Enablement platform, including identity protocols, APIs, SDKs, docs, examples, internal tooling, partner-debugging workflows, launch guardrails, and user-facing consent or control experiences. Work closely with product, engineering, design, partnerships, legal, policy, security, support, and go-to-market teams to make partner launches smooth, safe, and repeatable. Bring structured signals from partners back to product and engineering, and turn recurring integration patterns into platform requirements, reference architectures, playbooks, and developer guidance. Have built and operated production full-stack products, APIs, backend services, developer platforms, connectors, or integrations, and can reason across frontend, backend, auth, data models, reliability, privacy, and UX constraints. Have a strong understanding of how plugins and connectors work with coding agents, integrating MCP servers, using CLIs and APIs to access external tools. Can work comfortably with external engineers, product leaders, and executives, and translate partner feedback into crisp technical plans and product improvements. Are comfortable with ambiguity and rapidly changing conditions, and can turn high-level ideas into runnable prototypes, API contracts, technical specs. You will identify high-value user journeys, choose the right integration path, prototype and review architectures, write code, run evaluations and dogfood, trace failures end to end, guide launch and rollout, and support post-launch iteration. The best person for this role moves fluidly between full-stack code, OAuth/OIDC and identity systems, product judgment, project leadership, and clear communication with engineers and executives.

This role is a fit for a product-minded engineer who wants to stay close to users and partners while going deep on authentication, permissions, reliability, safety, and developer experience. The principle objective is to help partners ship low-friction, trustworthy agent experiences that work across real-world account states, enterprise constraints, and user expectations.

This role is based in our San Francisco office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the technical partner journey for priority agent enablement integrations—from use-case selection and readiness assessment through architecture, prototype, implementation, evaluation, launch, rollout, and ongoing maintenance.

 - Help partners choose and implement the right integration path across browser sign-in, connector-initiated OAuth, and agentic account linking or provisioning, with clear user journeys and safe fallback behavior.

 - Write production and sample code, build reference implementations and test harnesses, and create the technical guidance, integration checklists, evaluations, and debugging tools that move partners from concept to production.

 - Debug identity and agent workflows end to end: user interface state, browser redirects, PKCE/OIDC transactions, token exchange and validation, account mapping, connector callbacks, CLI or MCP handoffs, latency, retries, rate limits, logs, traces, and metrics.

 - Review partner architectures and implementation plans for API contracts, scopes and permissions, consent, terms acceptance, and account policy, secret handling, data boundaries, privacy, reliability, and long-term maintainability.

 - Run hands-on evaluations, dogfood, launch-readiness reviews, staged rollouts, and post-launch investigations; turn findings into concrete fixes rather than one-off workarounds.

 - Contribute targeted improvements to ChatGPT, Codex, and the Agent Enablement platform, including identity protocols, APIs, SDKs, docs, examples, internal tooling, partner-debugging workflows, launch guardrails, and user-facing consent or control experiences.

 - Work closely with product, engineering, design, partnerships, legal, policy, security, support, and go-to-market teams to make partner launches smooth, safe, and repeatable.

 - Bring structured signals from partners back to product and engineering, and turn recurring integration patterns into platform requirements, reference architectures, playbooks, and developer guidance.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 4–6 years of professional software engineering or AI engineering experience and are strong enough technically to contribute to the platform itself while still enjoying hands-on coding.

 - Have operated in a customer or partner facing roles in scoping projects, building MVPs, presenting trade-offs in solution design and architecture, understanding user value drivers as well as scoping and executing on tight implementation plans.

 - Have built and operated production full-stack products, APIs, backend services, developer platforms, connectors, or integrations, and can reason across frontend, backend, auth, data models, reliability, privacy, and UX constraints.

 - Have a strong understanding of how plugins and connectors work with coding agents, integrating MCP servers, using CLIs and APIs to access external tools.

 - Can work comfortably with external engineers, product leaders, and executives, and translate partner feedback into crisp technical plans and product improvements.

 - Are comfortable with ambiguity and rapidly changing conditions, and can turn high-level ideas into runnable prototypes, API contracts, technical specs.

 - Balance urgency with judgment and can keep complex partner launches moving while staying precise about the details that matter.

Preferred qualifications:

 - High-level understanding of the identity stack, including how OAuth works.

 - Experience designing or operating APIs, webhooks, schemas, SDKs, CLIs, MCP servers, tool-calling systems, or other developer-facing integrations.

 - Prior customer-facing or partner-facing engineering experience, including leading technical calls, navigating ambiguity, and helping external teams ship production software.

 - Strong familiarity with AI products, LLM APIs, ChatGPT or Codex surfaces, coding harnesses, developer platforms, agent workflows, or ecosystem products.

About the Role

Our Government Sales team has a unique mission to help the U.S. Intelligence Community understand the transformative impact that highly capable AI models can bring to its most critical missions. This role combines technical understanding, strategic vision, relationship management, and value-driven sales strategy tailored specifically to Intelligence Community customers.

You’ll drive key opportunities throughout the full sales cycle, from pipeline generation through deployment and expansion. You’ll collaborate closely with researchers, engineers, solution strategists, and cross-functional partners to help Intelligence Community customers advance their missions through AI.

This role is based in Washington, D.C. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In addition, this role requires frequent on-site engagement at customer and partner facilities across the Washington, D.C./Northern Virginia corridor, including classified environments.

In this role, you will:

  • Manage a focused set of key U.S. Intelligence Community accounts, developing and executing comprehensive account strategies.

  • Lead Intelligence Community customers through their AI adoption journey, from initial consideration through successful deployment and expansion.

  • Build trusted relationships with senior leaders, mission owners, technical stakeholders, acquisition professionals, and other decision-makers across the Intelligence Community.

  • Partner with Solutions and Research Engineering teams to design and execute complex customer programs and deployments.

  • Develop and execute capture and co-sell strategies with federal systems integrators and specialized mission partners to position OpenAI in multi-year programs of record.

  • Align opportunity planning and deal strategy to MIP and NIP funding cycles, classified contract vehicles, appropriations timing, and extended approval chains.

  • Work with cleared technical teams to demonstrate value across cloud, hybrid, on-premises, and air-gapped environments and translate technical fit into mission outcomes.

  • Own and manage an Intelligence Community consumption revenue target.

  • Develop pipeline, lead complex deal strategies, and drive opportunities through the full sales cycle.

  • Oversee revenue forecasting, pipeline management, and account reporting.

  • Analyze account performance and provide actionable insights to internal and external stakeholders.

  • Closely monitor Intelligence Community priorities, policies, acquisition trends, competitors, and partners to inform product roadmaps and company strategy.

  • Navigate complex security, compliance, procurement, and contracting requirements associated with Intelligence Community customers.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Solutions, Product, Engineering, Government Affairs, Marketing, Communications, Business Operations, People Operations, Finance, and Legal.

  • Support the recruitment and onboarding of team members focused on the Intelligence Community.

  • Help build and strengthen OpenAI’s culture and operating model within the Intelligence Community practice.

We're seeking someone with experience including:

  • 10+ years selling commercial technology, including platform-as-a-service, software-as-a-service, cloud, data, cybersecurity, or other enterprise technology, to the U.S. Intelligence Community.

  • A documented track record of closing high-value, multi-stakeholder enterprise technology deals across major Intelligence Community organizations and their supporting ecosystems.

  • An active Top Secret clearance with Full Scope Polygraph.

  • Developing and executing complex account and deal strategies within the Intelligence Community.

  • Navigating Intelligence Community procurement, acquisition, contracting, security, and deployment processes.

  • Deep familiarity with MIP and NIP funding cycles, classified contract vehicles, multi-year programs of record, and extended acquisition timelines.

  • An established senior-level network of GS-15/SES/SIS and C-suite relationships across major Intelligence Community organizations and their supporting ecosystems.

  • Experience partnering with federal systems integrators and specialized mission partners on capture strategies, co-selling, and program expansion.

  • Proven experience selling cloud, cybersecurity, hybrid-cloud, or AI infrastructure into sensitive or classified environments, including on-premises and air-gapped deployment patterns.

  • Consistently delivering growth in fast-paced, high-performance environments.

  • Working directly with senior Intelligence Community executives, mission leaders, technical stakeholders, and decision-makers.

  • Deep relationships and native familiarity with Intelligence Community missions, organizational structures, workflows, and buying processes.

  • Translating technical capabilities into clear mission outcomes and strategic value.

  • Communicating technical and strategic concepts clearly to both Intelligence Community customers and internal stakeholders.

  • Leading high-visibility customer briefings, executive engagements, demonstrations, and industry events.

  • Gathering, distilling, and applying detailed market intelligence, including agency priorities, policy developments, budget trends, acquisition strategies, and competitor activity.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are customer-centric. You are motivated to deeply understand defense customers’ priorities and help them achieve their mission-critical objectives using AI. You build trusted relationships with senior executives and stakeholders across defense and national security agencies.

  • Have a passion or deep curiosity about artificial intelligence. You embrace the opportunity to help deploy OpenAI’s technology in ways that advance national security missions and benefit humanity. You’re enthusiastic about educating defense customers on AI capabilities and strategic implications.

  • Are a builder. You enjoy impacting how our company grows its defense and intelligence business. You excel in establishing robust systems and processes tailored to defense customer requirements, executing them with precision and agility.

  • Are excited by new challenges. You thrive when solving complex, mission-critical defense and national security problems. Bespoke challenges requiring multidimensional knowledge excite you, and you’re eager to experiment with innovative solutions within national security environments.

  • Are a strategist. You deeply understand defense go-to-market best practices and proactively contribute to strategic initiatives. You plan years ahead, effectively aligning internal and external defense and intelligence stakeholders to achieve long-term objectives.

You will turn a deep understanding of this audience into positioning, experiences, and programs that earn genuine relevance and participation. records.title: Strategic Cloud Partner Enablement Lead
records.text: About the Role We are looking for a senior partner success and learning professional to activate cloud partners to co-sell and deploy customer solutions at scale. This role leads the enablement strategy and execution that equip partner teams to turn joint priorities into measurable customer and business outcomes. As a trusted advisor to strategic partners, you will turn shared business priorities into practical enablement programs that help partner sales, technical, customer success, and leadership teams identify joint opportunities, co-sell effectively, and deploy customer solutions successfully. You will own the partner enablement relationship for an assigned portfolio and work across internal teams to ensure programs are coordinated, scalable, and connected to measurable partner, customer, and business outcomes. This is not a traditional training delivery role or a quota-carrying partner account manager position. It is a consultative, partner-facing role for someone who can shape strategy, build relationships, translate complex AI capabilities into effective learning experiences, lead persuasive enablement sessions, and guide strategic partners toward sustained success. In this role, you will: Own strategic partner enablement and success Serve as the primary enablement and success lead for a portfolio of strategic cloud platforms. Develop a deep understanding of each partner’s business, priorities, audiences, existing learning infrastructure, and strategic relationship with our company. Build partner-specific enablement strategies aligned to shared goals, priorities, and the broader partnership strategy. Establish trusted relationships with partner leaders, alliance teams, enablement stakeholders, sales organizations, technical communities, and post-sales teams. Lead ongoing planning conversations, enablement reviews, stakeholder check-ins, and executive updates that keep partners and internal teams aligned. Identify gaps, risks, opportunities, and emerging partner needs, then coordinate the right response across internal and partner stakeholders. Design and deliver relevant learning programs Translate partner priorities, product capabilities, customer use cases, and go-to-market objectives into clear learning strategies and practical enablement plans. Create and manage differentiated learning pathways for partner sellers, solutions architects, developers, customer success teams, services teams, and leaders. Develop and deliver scalable enablement experiences, including workshops, technical deep dives, executive briefings, office hours, train-the-trainer programs, partner communities, and reusable learning resources. Collaborate with subject matter experts to ensure learning content is accurate, audience-specific, and grounded in real customer and partner scenarios. Adapt programs for different partner business models, geographic regions, technical maturity levels, and strategic priorities. Build repeatable program frameworks while tailoring the partner experience where the relationship requires a more customized approach. Promote practical understanding of generative AI, responsible AI use, product capabilities, solution positioning, technical implementation considerations, and customer value. Drive co-sell, deployment, and strategic outcomes Activate partner sales, technical, and customer success teams with the knowledge, confidence, and practical skills to co-sell and deploy customer solutions at scale. Support partner readiness across technical, sales, customer success, and leadership audiences. Connect enablement activity to co-sell execution, successful customer deployments, partner engagement, and partner-influenced business outcomes. Develop partner champions and internal advocates who can extend learning and knowledge sharing across their organizations. Use partner feedback, stakeholder input, and program data to refine enablement approaches and remove barriers to success. Ensure partner teams can access the resources, experts, and support they need to participate effectively in strategic initiatives. Lead through cross-functional partnership Work closely with strategic alliances, partner management, sales, solutions architecture, product, developer relations, customer success, marketing, and learning teams. Translate product launches, strategic initiatives, and evolving partner priorities into coordinated enablement actions. Represent the voice of the partner internally, sharing practical feedback on learning needs, content gaps, product questions, and program effectiveness. Coordinate across teams to deliver a cohesive experience without duplicating existing partner management, account ownership, or sales responsibilities. Influence stakeholders at multiple levels, from individual contributors and technical experts to senior partner executives. Measure and improve program effectiveness Establish clear measures for partner engagement, training attendance, workshops delivered, badges earned, stakeholder participation, and program reach. Monitor trends across partner audiences, geographies, learning pathways, and strategic initiatives to identify where additional support is needed. Maintain a clear view of partner enablement priorities, program status, partner feedback, and progress against shared goals. Communicate program insights and outcomes through concise partner updates, business reviews, and leadership reporting. Continuously improve learning experiences based on participation, partner feedback, observed readiness, and strategic business impact. You might thrive in this role if you have: 8+ years of experience in partner success, strategic partnerships, partner enablement, customer success, learning and development, or consulting within enterprise technology. Proven success managing strategic partner relationships and designing and delivering enablement programs that improve partner readiness and business outcomes. Strong understanding of cloud, enterprise software, or AI technologies, with the ability to translate complex concepts for technical and business audiences. Experience partnering across sales, solutions architecture, product, customer success, alliances, and other cross-functional teams. Strong consulting, facilitation, presentation, relationship management, and program management skills. Comfort working with senior stakeholders and navigating global partner organizations, competing priorities, and multiple audiences. A practical, data-informed approach to measuring partner engagement, readiness, co-sell execution, customer deployments, and business impact. Sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, adaptability, and a genuine interest in helping strategic partners succeed. Helpful experience: Experience working with strategic cloud partners such as AWS, Google Cloud, and Oracle. Experience in generative AI, machine learning, cloud infrastructure, developer platforms, or enterprise AI adoption. Background in instructional design, adult learning, learning consulting, technical enablement, or enterprise learning program development. Experience building role-based learning pathways, partner champion programs, hands-on workshops, technical bootcamps, or train-the-trainer models. Experience supporting global partner programs across multiple regions, stakeholder groups, and levels of technical maturity. Familiarity with learning platforms, partner portals, CRM tools, dashboards, or other systems used to manage partner enablement and engagement. How success is measured: Strategic partners have clear, mutually understood enablement priorities and an active plan aligned to the partnership strategy. Partner sales, technical, customer success, and leadership audiences participate in relevant learning opportunities. Training attendance, workshops delivered, badges, partner engagement, and stakeholder coverage show meaningful progress. Partner teams demonstrate stronger product understanding and readiness to identify joint opportunities, co-sell effectively, and deploy customer solutions. Partner stakeholders view the enablement relationship as valuable, responsive, and aligned to their business needs. Internal teams have a clear view of partner priorities, program performance, emerging needs, and opportunities for improvement. Enablement contributes to increased co-sell activity, successful customer deployments, stronger strategic partnerships, and partner-influenced growth. original.title: Strategic Cloud Partner Enablement Lead
original.descriptionHtml:
About the Role

We are looking for a senior partner success and learning professional to activate cloud partners to co-sell and deploy customer solutions at scale. This role leads the enablement strategy and execution that equip partner teams to turn joint priorities into measurable customer and business outcomes.

As a trusted advisor to strategic partners, you will turn shared business priorities into practical enablement programs that help partner sales, technical, customer success, and leadership teams identify joint opportunities, co-sell effectively, and deploy customer solutions successfully. You will own the partner enablement relationship for an assigned portfolio and work across internal teams to ensure programs are coordinated, scalable, and connected to measurable partner, customer, and business outcomes.

This is not a traditional training delivery role or a quota-carrying partner account manager position. It is a consultative, partner-facing role for someone who can shape strategy, build relationships, translate complex AI capabilities into effective learning experiences, lead persuasive enablement sessions, and guide strategic partners toward sustained success.


In this role, you will:

Own strategic partner enablement and success

  • Serve as the primary enablement and success lead for a portfolio of strategic cloud platforms.

  • Develop a deep understanding of each partner’s business, priorities, audiences, existing learning infrastructure, and strategic relationship with our company.

  • Build partner-specific enablement strategies aligned to shared goals, priorities, and the broader partnership strategy.

  • Establish trusted relationships with partner leaders, alliance teams, enablement stakeholders, sales organizations, technical communities, and post-sales teams.

  • Lead ongoing planning conversations, enablement reviews, stakeholder check-ins, and executive updates that keep partners and internal teams aligned.

  • Identify gaps, risks, opportunities, and emerging partner needs, then coordinate the right response across internal and partner stakeholders.

Design and deliver relevant learning programs

  • Translate partner priorities, product capabilities, customer use cases, and go-to-market objectives into clear learning strategies and practical enablement plans.

  • Create and manage differentiated learning pathways for partner sellers, solutions architects, developers, customer success teams, services teams, and leaders.

  • Develop and deliver scalable enablement experiences, including workshops, technical deep dives, executive briefings, office hours, train-the-trainer programs, partner communities, and reusable learning resources.

  • Collaborate with subject matter experts to ensure learning content is accurate, audience-specific, and grounded in real customer and partner scenarios.

  • Adapt programs for different partner business models, geographic regions, technical maturity levels, and strategic priorities.

  • Build repeatable program frameworks while tailoring the partner experience where the relationship requires a more customized approach.

  • Promote practical understanding of generative AI, responsible AI use, product capabilities, solution positioning, technical implementation considerations, and customer value.

Drive co-sell, deployment, and strategic outcomes

  • Activate partner sales, technical, and customer success teams with the knowledge, confidence, and practical skills to co-sell and deploy customer solutions at scale.

  • Support partner readiness across technical, sales, customer success, and leadership audiences.

  • Connect enablement activity to co-sell execution, successful customer deployments, partner engagement, and partner-influenced business outcomes.

  • Develop partner champions and internal advocates who can extend learning and knowledge sharing across their organizations.

  • Use partner feedback, stakeholder input, and program data to refine enablement approaches and remove barriers to success.

  • Ensure partner teams can access the resources, experts, and support they need to participate effectively in strategic initiatives.

Lead through cross-functional partnership

  • Work closely with strategic alliances, partner management, sales, solutions architecture, product, developer relations, customer success, marketing, and learning teams.

  • Translate product launches, strategic initiatives, and evolving partner priorities into coordinated enablement actions.

  • Represent the voice of the partner internally, sharing practical feedback on learning needs, content gaps, product questions, and program effectiveness.

  • Coordinate across teams to deliver a cohesive experience without duplicating existing partner management, account ownership, or sales responsibilities.

  • Influence stakeholders at multiple levels, from individual contributors and technical experts to senior partner executives.

Measure and improve program effectiveness

  • Establish clear measures for partner engagement, training attendance, workshops delivered, badges earned, stakeholder participation, and program reach.

  • Monitor trends across partner audiences, geographies, learning pathways, and strategic initiatives to identify where additional support is needed.

  • Maintain a clear view of partner enablement priorities, program status, partner feedback, and progress against shared goals.

  • Communicate program insights and outcomes through concise partner updates, business reviews, and leadership reporting.

  • Continuously improve learning experiences based on participation, partner feedback, observed readiness, and strategic business impact.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 8+ years of experience in partner success, strategic partnerships, partner enablement, customer success, learning and development, or consulting within enterprise technology.

  • Proven success managing strategic partner relationships and designing and delivering enablement programs that improve partner readiness and business outcomes.

  • Strong understanding of cloud, enterprise software, or AI technologies, with the ability to translate complex concepts for technical and business audiences.

  • Experience partnering across sales, solutions architecture, product, customer success, alliances, and other cross-functional teams.

  • Strong consulting, facilitation, presentation, relationship management, and program management skills.

  • Comfort working with senior stakeholders and navigating global partner organizations, competing priorities, and multiple audiences.

  • A practical, data-informed approach to measuring partner engagement, readiness, co-sell execution, customer deployments, and business impact.

  • Sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, adaptability, and a genuine interest in helping strategic partners succeed.

Helpful experience:

  • Experience working with strategic cloud partners such as AWS, Google Cloud, and Oracle.

  • Experience in generative AI, machine learning, cloud infrastructure, developer platforms, or enterprise AI adoption.

  • Background in instructional design, adult learning, learning consulting, technical enablement, or enterprise learning program development.

  • Experience building role-based learning pathways, partner champion programs, hands-on workshops, technical bootcamps, or train-the-trainer models.

  • Experience supporting global partner programs across multiple regions, stakeholder groups, and levels of technical maturity.

  • Familiarity with learning platforms, partner portals, CRM tools, dashboards, or other systems used to manage partner enablement and engagement.

How success is measured:

  • Strategic partners have clear, mutually understood enablement priorities and an active plan aligned to the partnership strategy.

  • Partner sales, technical, customer success, and leadership audiences participate in relevant learning opportunities.

  • Training attendance, workshops delivered, badges, partner engagement, and stakeholder coverage show meaningful progress.

  • Partner teams demonstrate stronger product understanding and readiness to identify joint opportunities, co-sell effectively, and deploy customer solutions.

  • Partner stakeholders view the enablement relationship as valuable, responsive, and aligned to their business needs.

  • Internal teams have a clear view of partner priorities, program performance, emerging needs, and opportunities for improvement.

  • Enablement contributes to increased co-sell activity, successful customer deployments, stronger strategic partnerships, and partner-influenced growth.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link.

  • Support model design, ownership, SLAs, escalation paths, and lifecycle management

It is a hands-on governance and enablement role that partners with business teams, IT operations, Security, Procurement, Business Platforms, Applied teams and Data Engineering to guide software decisions, reduce unmanaged sprawl, and build reusable enterprise foundations.



Why This Role Matters

OpenAI’s software footprint is expanding rapidly across SaaS, internally built tools, agents, integrations, APIs, third-party platforms, and application systems that OpenAI. The company needs a stronger tools architecture layer that can help teams make good decisions early, avoid duplicate tools, govern sensitive data and identities, and identify where OpenAI should build instead of buy.

The person in this role will help turn software governance from an approval checkpoint into an enterprise capability: a system that improves speed, reliability, security, and business outcomes.



What You'll Do

 - Own the target architecture for enterprise software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, and agent-enabled business systems across Corporate IT.  Drive deprecation and consolidate targets for enterprise software.

 - Build lightweight governance patterns that guide teams before software and integration decisions become hard to unwind.

 - Create architecture standards for identity, access, data movement, API usage, admin rights, auditability, observability, and vendor integration.

 - Partner with Security to ensure software architecture addresses SSO, SCIM, MFA, privileged access, non-human identities, secrets, token storage, data residency, encryption, retention, and incident response readiness.

 - Partner with Procurement and Finance to evaluate renewals, rationalization opportunities, enterprise agreements, and build-versus-buy decisions.

 - Partner deeply with application verticals such as GTM, Finance, Legal, HR, Research, Product, and Operations teams to evaluate agentic business workflows and translate them into scalable enterprise system patterns.

 - Review proposed SaaS and internally built tools for overlap, risk, integration quality, ownership, lifecycle, supportability, and long-term fit.

 - Develop reusable architecture blueprints for common capabilities such as intake, workflow, approvals, knowledge management, customer/partner 360, data integration, reporting, content management, learning, surveys, and collaboration.

 - Help define where OpenAI-native GPT or agent-built solutions should replace or enable point SaaS tools.

 - Create clear decision records and architecture artifacts that are understandable by business leaders, engineers, security reviewers, and procurement partners.

 - Drive software catalog maturity by connecting tool inventory, business owner, system owner, integration path, data classification, access model, renewal, risk posture, and support model.



Core Architecture Domains

 - SaaS governance and software catalog maturity

 - Enterprise integration architecture, including APIs, event flows, middleware, and system-of-record boundaries

 - Identity, access, and admin model design across internal and external users

 - Data architecture for SaaS, customer, supplier, employee, partner, product, consumption, and connected business models.

 - Agentic workflow architecture and GPT-built replacement patterns

 - Vendor architecture reviews and enterprise agreement leverage across strategic platforms.

 - Security, compliance, ITGC, audit evidence, and operational readiness

 - Support model design, ownership, SLAs, escalation paths, and lifecycle management



What You'll Bring

 - 10+ years of experience in enterprise architecture, business systems architecture, IT architecture, SaaS governance, integration architecture, or a related technical leadership role.

 - Strong understanding of SaaS operating models, software lifecycle management, software asset management, and vendor/platform governance.

 - Experience designing integrations across systems, experience in large scale SaaS such as CRM, ERP and Marketplace platforms.

 - Practical knowledge of identity and access patterns including SSO, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, RBAC/ABAC, privileged admin models, service accounts, OAuth apps, and token governance.

 - Ability to evaluate software from multiple angles: business value, architecture fit, security posture, data exposure, cost, supportability, user experience, and vendor strategy.

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity, building structure where little exists, and influencing senior stakeholders without relying only on formal authority.

 - Ability to write clear architecture decision records, governance standards, system diagrams, business cases, and executive-ready recommendations.

 - Strong partner orientation: able to help teams move faster while raising the quality of decisions.

 - Curiosity about AI-native enterprise architecture and where GPT, Codex, and agentic workflows can replace or enable traditional SaaS patterns.

 - Experience scaling IT or business systems from startup-stage tooling into mature enterprise architecture.

 - Experience with software rationalization, SaaS enablement and deprecation, vendor consolidation, or enterprise license optimization.

 - Experience with architecting systems in a high-growth environment.
